analysis:
Compared complete supplied route/watchdog BASE and HEAD source, patches and file metadata; examined the desktop concurrency patch. No concrete security regression is established. darkbloom-route.yml:86-88 bounds attempts to 1–9; :187-244 adds bounded retry/backoff and allowlisted JSON diagnostics. HTTPS-only transport, five-second attempts, body limits, fork exclusion, empty permissions and exact runner-label matching (:274) remain intact. Response header values cannot become shell commands, and configuration diagnostics now strip CR/LF/% (:80-82). Requests still disclose only repository/run/lane metadata, not provider credentials or consumer plaintext.

darkbloom-watchdog.yml:241-245 now suppresses automatic cancellation whenever a current-attempt Darkbloom job has a runner, is in progress or succeeded, including previously failed jobs retaining runner identity. This deliberately reduces fallback reruns and their cost, but also removes this workflow's recovery for partially executed attempts with stranded queued shards. GitHub-token permissions, marker handling and cancellation/rerun APIs are otherwise unchanged. Integration should reconcile that availability tradeoff with the platform watchdog; its current implementation is not supplied.

desktop.yml:23-26 cancels superseded runs within workflow/PR-or-ref groups. Remaining jobs and triggers are absent: integration must verify cancellation cleanup and whether any artifact publication or qualification work shares this workflow. Also confirm the plane's repeated-POST allocation/idempotency contract for the increased retry budget; missing backend evidence is not a finding. The indexed A-011/A-017 and T-054 build-integrity contracts are relevant if desktop produces qualified artifacts. No supplied change touches inference encryption, authorization, cache isolation (T-041), attestation or billing-ledger controls. CI rescue is distinct from the provider rollback watchdog in T-043. This is local source coverage, not clearance of callers or external services.
